lots.what_it_is: Single strand of about 40 large near-round white pearls (very roughly 10-11mm, only slight graduation), knotted, on a small gold spring-ring clasp stamped 750 (18ct). Catalogued as 10.5mm South Sea pearls on an 18K clasp. The 750 stamp is clearly legible in photo 2. Several pearls show the rippled, slightly off-round surface and pink-blue overtones typical of modern bead-nucleated (Edison-type) freshwater pearls, so the South Seas claim is not supported by the photos and should be treated as unproven.

lots.working: No SOLD evidence, so keep_max_hammer = 0 and flip_max_hammer = 0. Gowans premium 19.8% (all-in = hammer x 1.198). The 18ct clasp is a small spring ring, likely well under 1g, so it adds only a few dollars of gold value. Any value rests on the pearls; if freshwater, large round strands of this kind usually trade cheaply second-hand, but I have no verified price to show, so no bid is set.
lots.confidence_reason: 750 clasp mark read, but pearl type (freshwater vs South Sea) cannot be confirmed from photos and there is no price evidence of any kind.

lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 1: about 40 white pearls, near-round with visible surface ripples and wrinkles on several, strong lustre, pink and blue overtones, knotted between each pearl, little graduation. Photo 2: gold spring-ring clasp stamped 750, attached to a short length of flat twisted gold chain; no maker's mark seen.
lots.condition: Appears clean with good lustre; knotting looks intact in the photos. Surface blemishes and ripples visible on several pearls. Strand length not stated.
lots.question_for_gowans: What is the basis for calling these South Sea pearls (any certificate or lab report)? What is the strand length and the measured pearl size? Is the clasp the only gold (and does it close securely), and is the stringing sound?
